mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above 4.5% in the month preceding the prediction triggers a risk-off reaction, depressing near-term equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.5% in the preceding month
regime_hint: tightening phase of the Fed Funds rate
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat despite FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in a 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which tends to boost equity valuations and drive positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE decreases in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when the labor strength signal is present.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months indicates accelerating economic demand, which is associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite INDPRO being above MA for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in manufacturing activity (HOUST) accompanied by a decline in consumer demand proxy (GDPC1) suggests overcapacity and weak fundamentals, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when both indicators show contraction.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for two consecutive months indicates disinflation, which typically precedes a shift to rate cuts and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are flat or negative despite CPIAUCSL < 3% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in job openings reported by PAYEMS exceeding 200,000 in a month while UNRATE remains below 4% indicates a labor market imbalance favoring demand, which tends to drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 200,000 and UNRATE < 4% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive when the labor tightness signal is present.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in consumer confidence proxy (not available in the given catalog) cannot be used; instead, a sustained drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 for three months suggests supply-side weakness, predicting negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative despite INDPRO < 100 for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5% triggers a risk aversion wave as investors anticipate further policy tightening, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 5% in the current month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or flat despite UNRATE > 5% in the current month.
